item.text: {"confident":true,"explanation":"A d'Alembert equation has the form y = xf(y') + g(y'). Equation I already has this form. Equation II rearranges to y = -x(y')^2 + 2^{y'}, so it also qualifies. Equation III gives y = x/(y' - x^2), which cannot be expressed in the required form.","answers":[{"key":"selection","correct_option":"d","correct_value":"I and II only","value_type":"text","wrong_value":"II and III only","correct_keys":[],"wrong_keys":[]}]}
